newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian 10-year OLO yld seen below 6.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgian 10-year OLO yld seen below 6.00 pct.

text.p: OLOs are poised to extend their recent rally once the uncertainty of the Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting on Wednesday is out of the way and provided it results in unchanged U.S. interest rates as expected, dealers said.
"The market has discounted that there will be no change, and we are quite bullish," said one dealer, citing further upward potential for U.S. long bonds as a reason for optimism.

The 10-year benchmark 2006 OLO yield finished at 6.01 percent, just a basis point below the previous close after a tightly traded session. Several dealers predicted the yield would fall below 6.00 percent, perhaps as early as Thursday.
The prospect of the FOMC meeting, still in progress when the Belgian market closed, was responsible for Wednesday's low activity, dealers said.
"Five years outperformed 10 years in the morning but that reversed in the afternoon, and we saw half the normal volume of trading," one noted.

The ten year yield premium over Bunds edged in two basis points to 15 bp. Some dealers said they were happy with current levels, and that last month's spreads of six, seven and eight basis points had been too low for comfort. Others predicted further widening, with buyers coming around the 20 level.
Belgian bond futures ended 0.03 point up on the previous close at 120.06 after opening at a new contract high of 120.14.
U.S. October consumer prices will give the market a focal point on Thursday, with prices expected to show a year-on-year rise of 3.0 percent - unchanged from the previous month.
